analyses.spec_says: spec/m_apb_tlul_bridge_Design_Specification.md:128 REQ-ERR-001: "When a write has PSTRB other than 4'b1111, the bridge shall issue no TL-UL request and shall complete the transfer with PREADY = 1 and PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle." Spec line 398 defines the internal signal: "w_legal | i_apb_paddr[1:0] = 2'b00 and (i_apb_pwrite = 0 or i_apb_pstrb = 4'b1111)". Line 164 says the Setup/legality block "checks PSTRB and PADDR[1:0]". Line 470 ERR-001 / rules.json BR-12-01 (line 3836): "Write with PSTRB other than 4'b1111; ... PREADY = 1 and PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle; PRDATA = 0; no TL-UL request". DEC-001 (line 696) confirms this. contract.json:473 (CHK-007) uses illegal = (paddr[1:0]!=0) or (pwrite==1 and pstrb!=4'b1111).
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_apb_if.sv:66 `assign w_legal = (i_apb_paddr[1:0] == 2'b00);` checks only alignment. The comment on lines 64-65 says it also needs "a full strobe when the access is a write", but i_apb_pstrb (port at line 26) is never used. So for an aligned write with PSTRB=0 at the Setup edge E0: w_req_launch=1 and w_local_err=0 (lines 69-70). The APB FSM goes IDLE->BUSY (line 91) instead of DONE. reg_pready/reg_pslverr stay 0 (lines 108-109, 139-140). m_tlul_if loads channel A (w_load, m_tlul_if.sv:89, 153, 180), so at E1 o_tlul_a_valid=1. This is exactly the observed pready=0 pslverr=0 a_valid=1.
analyses.test_does: verif/tests/test_apb_tlul_bridge.py:724 builds illegal writes `Transfer(1, aligned(q), ..., s, ...)` for s in range(15). The first transfer is an aligned write with PSTRB=4'b0000. Each is followed by a legal full-strobe write (line 730). The scoreboard sets the expectation at lines 264-270: legal = paddr[1:0]==0 and (pwrite==0 or pstrb==0xF), and _setup_illegal = setup and not legal. Lines 217-220 then assert pready=1, pslverr=1, prdata=0, a_valid=0 at E1. This legality formula is the same as the one in spec line 398 and contract CHK-007.

candidates.evidence_for: m_apb_if.sv:66 leaves out the `(~i_apb_pwrite | i_apb_pstrb==4'b1111)` term that is required by spec line 398, REQ-ERR-001 (line 128), DEC-001 (line 696) and the RTL's own comment (lines 64-65). i_apb_pstrb is a port of m_apb_if (line 26) and is wired from the top (m_apb_tlul_bridge.sv:96), but no logic uses it. The failing stimulus is an aligned write with PSTRB=0, which only the missing term can reject. The observed values (a_valid=1, pready=0) match the launch path exactly.
candidates.evidence_against: None found. Misaligned accesses go through the implemented term, and CHK-007 has hits=5 with fails=4 (sim.log:224), so one illegal Setup passed. That fits only the strobe term being missing.

analyses.spec_says: contract.json:473: "Let illegal = (i_apb_paddr[1:0]!=2'b00) or (i_apb_pwrite==1 and i_apb_pstrb!=4'b1111). ... then at E1: o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=1, o_apb_prdata=32'h0 and o_tlul_a_valid=0; and at E2: o_tlul_a_valid=0." spec:128 REQ-ERR-001; spec:129 REQ-ERR-002; spec:409 OP-003 "APB write with PSTRB other than 4'b1111, or any access with PADDR[1:0] not 2'b00 | No TL-UL request | PREADY = 1 with PSLVERR = 1, PRDATA = 0 | 1 Access cycle"; rules.json BR-T1-03 (line 41).
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_apb_if.sv:66 computes legality from alignment only, so w_local_err (line 70) is 0 for an aligned write with a partial strobe. The local-error branch (lines 111-114: pready=1, pslverr=1, prdata=0) and the IDLE->DONE transition (line 93) are never taken for that case. Instead, the request is launched (lines 69, 73, 91). Misaligned accesses do take the local-error path. This fits hits=5 / fails=4: the one passing hit is consistent with a misaligned illegal Setup.

Lines 110-112 assert `(psel && !penable && w_illegal) |=> (pready && pslverr && prdata==0 && !a_valid) ##1 !a_valid`. The illegal-strobe writes come from tests 018 (PSTRB=0, test line 724), 025 (PSTRB=0x3, line 973), 028 (PSTRB=0x5, line 1097) and 029 (random).

candidates.evidence_for: The checker's illegal formula equals the spec (spec:398 negated) and the contract (contract.json:473). The RTL's legality at m_apb_if.sv:66 is missing the write-strobe term, and i_apb_pstrb is unused in m_apb_if, contradicting the module's own comment (lines 64-65) and spec:164 ("checks PSTRB and PADDR[1:0]"). All 4 fails coincide with CHK-014 fails, i.e. a request was launched.
None. The checker is disabled in reset and uses only ports, and the antecedent is the plain Setup level with illegal inputs.
candidates.evidence_against: The formula matches contract and spec exactly. The one passing hit shows the consequent timing (E1 local error, E2 no a_valid) is right for the RTL's implemented path.

Spec, DEC-001 (designer-confirmed, spec:696) and rules.json Q&A (line ~7552-7553: "A read ignores PSTRB, so any PSTRB value on a read is accepted") all agree that only writes with a partial strobe are illegal. That is exactly the case that fails.

analyses.options: Fix RTL: in rtl/m_apb_if.sv:66 add the write-strobe term: `assign w_legal = (i_apb_paddr[1:0] == 2'b00) & (~i_apb_pwrite | (i_apb_pstrb == 4'b1111));`. With this, w_local_err drives the existing local-error path (lines 92-93, 111-114) for partial-strobe writes. This single change should clear all six reported failures. No checker, test or spec change is indicated.
